extracted.intended_audience: PTAB practitioners, patent litigators, and intellectual property attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for handling inter partes reviews, patent eligibility, claim construction, stays, estoppel, mandamus, and related district-court procedures in patent litigation and PTAB proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of appeal issues not challenged in opening brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A party forfeits challenges (e.g., to an untimeliness holding) by failing to challenge them in its opening brief on appeal; an unchallenged ground (such as untimeliness) may constitute an independent, dispositive ground for affirmance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the petitioner did not challenge the Board’s untimeliness determination in the opening brief, the Federal Circuit treated that determination as an independent ground for decision and declined to reach the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation requires relevant disclosure by another inventor
rubrics_metrics.description: To show anticipation by a prior reference, the reference must be 'invented by another' person than the patent's inventor; if the relevant disclosure in the reference reproduces an earlier report written by the challenged patent’s named inventors, the inventors may be the same for anticipation purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look to who authored the relevant portions of the reference; identical underlying authorship can defeat a 'invented by another' anticipation theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product-by-process limitation weight
rubrics_metrics.description: A product-by-process limitation (e.g., 'cast in one piece') carries no patentable weight unless it is shown to impart any difference in structure from a product made otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the limitation does not change the product’s structure, it cannot distinguish the claim over prior art merely because of the described process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of § 315(e)(2) estoppel defined by petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Estoppel under 35 U.S.C. § 315(e)(2) is defined by the petition’s content — the petition, not the institution decision, defines the scope of the IPR for estoppel purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including a claim/ground in the petition can result in estoppel even if the Board denied institution on that ground; a petitioner should seek remand (e.g., under SAS) if institution error needs correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 315(e)(2) estoppel does not require actual litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Estoppel applies to grounds that 'reasonably could have [been] raised' and does not require that the issue have been 'actually litigated' in the IPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even non-instituted grounds included in a petition can trigger estoppel in later proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director discretionary review satisfies Appointments Clause
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director’s discretionary power to review institution/denial decisions (including sua sponte review) satisfies the Appointments Clause — delegation of institution authority to the Board is permissible where the Director retains review authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of mandamus is limited; courts may find the statutory/regulatory scheme constitutional if Director possesses review discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alice/Mayo § 101 eligibility — abstract idea/mental process
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims directed to collection/comprehension of information and indication of results, performable in the human mind and executed on a generic computer in its normal manner, are directed to an abstract idea and fail step one of Alice/Mayo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show specifically how asserted evidence (e.g., documents) alters the eligibility finding and include such evidence in the joint appendix to avoid forfeiture on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of evidentiary arguments on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments based on evidentiary submissions (e.g., documents submitted to examiner) are forfeited on appeal if the appellant does not explain what the documents show or include them in the joint appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include and cite specific evidence in the record and joint appendix to preserve factual/evidentiary arguments for appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of claim before final decision affects standing to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If a challenged claim is finally cancelled in a co-pending proceeding before the PTAB’s final written decision, the patent owner lacks standing to appeal the Board’s unpatentability determination as to that claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation prior to the final decision eliminates the concrete interest necessary to pursue appeal for that claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may derive level of ordinary skill from whole record
rubrics_metrics.description: Even where little supporting evidence is presented, the Board may reasonably determine the level of ordinary skill in the art from the whole record, especially when parties treat the issue conclusorily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should present focused evidence on level-of-skill questions rather than cursory treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherent anticipation 'limited class' / 'at once envisage' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Inherent anticipation requires that a skilled artisan may 'at once envisage each member of a limited class' disclosed by the reference; a disclosure of a very large or unpredictable class (e.g., 957 salts) is not a 'limited class' sufficient for inherent anticipation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where prior art lists many possible permutations and outcome (e.g., salt formation) is unpredictable, reliance on hindsight to pick one member is improper for anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fifth Circuit mandamus standard for transfer motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandamus is an extraordinary remedy reserved for extraordinary causes; in transfer contexts, review is only for clear abuses of discretion producing patently erroneous results. Parties seeking venue transfer must act with reasonable promptness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private interest factors (e.g., physical evidence location) and public interest factors (docket efficiency, court familiarity) guide transfer; delays in seeking transfer and whether evidence is electronic vs physical affect weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion-to-amend responsiveness requirement in IPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute claim in a motion to amend need only include at least one limitation that directly responds to a ground of unpatentability; the patentee may include other non-substantive amendments in the proposed substitute claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 42.121 does not require every amendment in the substitute claim to be directly responsive so long as at least one narrowing responsive limitation is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB not bound to accept argument-based disclaimer in IPR
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board is not required to treat a patent owner’s statements in an IPR as a binding disclaimer for determining claim scope — the PTO need not accept disclaimer-by-argument in the same IPR proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A disclaimer in an IPR is binding in later proceedings but not necessarily in the IPR itself; patentees should use the motion-to-amend process rather than rely on argument-based disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandamus to terminate ex parte reexamination requires clear, indisputable right
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandamus relief to terminate an ex parte reexamination is unavailable unless the petitioner shows a clear and indisputable right to such relief; post-final decision appeal can be an adequate remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts are reluctant to issue mandamus where the addition of references in reexamination is not 'so clearly contrary to law or the record' to warrant extraordinary relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral estoppel (issue preclusion) across IPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: A final PTAB decision in one IPR can create collateral estoppel in another IPR involving a related patent when the issue is identical, fully and fairly litigated, and essential to the earlier decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior IPR decision occurred after filing the later petition, the party may raise collateral estoppel on appeal even if not raised at the PTAB stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: District-court stay standard — good cause and case-specific factors
rubrics_metrics.description: A district court grants or denies stays pending PTAB proceedings based on factors including whether the stay will simplify issues, stage of litigation (e.g., claim construction completed, discovery stage), timing and diligence in filing IPRs, prejudice to plaintiff, and potential for delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts weigh early-stage litigation, lack of scheduling/trial date, and potential simplification in favor of a stay; speculative simplification, advanced stage, or prejudice (including imminent patent expiry) weigh against a stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic stay upon initial PTO rejection or third-party reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts do not adopt a bright-line rule granting stays simply because a PTO examiner initially rejected claims or a third party requested reexamination; delay in filing and risk of serial/never-ending reexaminations weigh against a stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stay may be denied when a requesting party 'drug its feet' in seeking reexamination or when the reexamination is unlikely to simplify the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial institution may still justify staying the case
rubrics_metrics.description: A stay may be granted even if only some of multiple petitions are instituted (e.g., 5 of 14), if review of those petitions is likely to simplify trial issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts consider whether instituted petitions target claims likely to affect the core litigation and whether other stay factors favor abstention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral estoppel limits expert testimony after PTAB invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Federal Circuit affirms a PTAB decision on particular factual findings about prior art, courts may bar experts from offering opinions that contradict those Board factual findings while allowing opinions on issues not invalidated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which factual findings were necessary to the PTAB judgment; experts cannot re-litigate those matters in district court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding or asserting new claims post-PTAB — showing good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: A plaintiff may be allowed to assert previously unasserted claims after PTAB proceedings if it shows good cause and reasonable diligence in seeking to assert them, and the defendant is not prejudiced (especially if PTAB fully reviewed those claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate diligence in discovery and explain why the new claims were not previously asserted; absence of prejudice to defendant favors permitting the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB analysis may inform indefiniteness determinations in district court
rubrics_metrics.description: A district court may rely on the PTAB’s ability to analyze a claim term in light of prior art and prosecution statements to conclude the term is not indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prosecution history and PTAB analyses as evidence of a term’s meaning; PTAB’s engagement with the claim term can support definiteness findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney’s fees and exceptional-case standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A court will not award attorney’s fees simply because a defendant previously succeeded in IPRs; a finding that the plaintiff’s litigation was frivolous or constituted exceptional conduct is required to justify fee awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to respond to PTO office actions or to litigate reasonably does not automatically render the case exceptional; courts exercise discretion based on totality of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery of costs despite partial PTAB invalidations
rubrics_metrics.description: A plaintiff who loses some patents in PTAB reviews but prevails on other asserted patents in district court may still recover costs if those remaining victories suffice to support an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidation or withdrawal of some patents does not necessarily defeat entitlement to costs for successful litigation on remaining claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial scheduling and PTAB timing — prejudice analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may deny requests to accelerate trial dates when pending PTAB petitions could be discretionarily denied and advancement would prejudice the responding party by foreclosing summary-judgment process or creating trial-preparation prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether shortening schedules would impair the ability to address potential PTAB outcomes and whether it would unfairly preclude dispositive motions.
